comparator.name: Rechtsgeleerdheid
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 OER defines a 180-EC bachelor: a 135-EC major and 45-EC profiling space. The major contains 67.5 EC of common compulsory study, including one 7.5-EC graduation project, plus one 67.5-EC route. The generic target names no route. The Multidisciplinary track is selected because it is the broad, least-specialised route and explicitly combines 67.5 EC of legal study with 45 EC of non-legal profiling; it requires Algemene rechtsleer and eight of ten listed legal choices. The neutral official-order rule selects the first eight choices, with Arbeidsrecht as the first-listed option inside Privaatrecht in perspectief. The 45-EC non-legal profiling space remains generic rather than being filled with invented subjects.

candidates.label: Private law, business and commercial relationships

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no internal route. The Multidisciplinary track is expressly designed to combine legal study with another field and reserves 45 EC for non-legal profiling, making it the broadest and least-specialised official route independently of UCR course availability.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic legal-foundations, rights, justice and social-change interests. Two generator-backed directions are feasible and materially distinct: public, international and European law, and private law, business and commercial relations. The three alternatives differ substantially in course composition and organising emphasis, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

alternatives.label: Law, politics & society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum combines its full available law sequence with politics, sociology, economics, philosophy, research and communication. The label states that interdisciplinary composition and does not imply a Dutch qualifying law degree.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines broad legal foundations and human rights with criminal, private, constitutional, international and EU law, supported by politics, sociology, economics, ethics, empirical research and persuasive communication.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every advanced law course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes the selected economics courses with that prerequisite. Introductory politics, sociology, economics and ethics precede advanced EU politics, social theory, public economics, conflict study and research. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Public, international & European law
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum concentrates constitutional and international law, EU law and politics, comparative institutions, conflict, history and social movements without implying a complete Dutch-law curriculum.
alternatives.concept: A public and cross-border legal direction connecting constitutional, international and EU law with comparative politics, international relations, EU institutions, conflict, history, sociology, public economics and qualitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal and private law, political philosophy, ethics, persuasive communication and negotiation. It adds business foundations, modern and imperial history, the history of warfare, international business governance and social-movement study. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising emphasis shifts to public institutions, cross-border orders and their historical and social contexts.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes constitutional, international and EU law. Comparative politics, international-relations theory, sociology, economics and research methods precede advanced EU politics, conflict, social theory, international governance and historical research. Business Foundations precedes International Business & Governance. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Private law, business & commercial relations
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines private and transnational business law with accounting, finance, economics, strategy, negotiation, research and communication; it does not overstate UCR’s private-law depth.
alternatives.concept: A private and commercial legal direction combining private, international, constitutional and EU law with transnational business law, accounting, finance, economics, strategy, organisational behaviour, negotiation and applied business research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal law, political philosophy, comparative politics, international-relations theory, EU politics, conflict studies, qualitative sociology and historical research. It adds business foundations, accounting and finance, digital strategy, organisational psychology, transnational business law, international business governance, econometrics and market research. Eleven courses differ from the closest match and twelve differ from the public/international route.
progression: Law, Society & Justice and Business Foundations establish the legal and commercial strands before advanced private, EU, transnational-business and international-governance courses. Research Methods & Statistics precedes negotiation, public economics, econometrics and market research. The final year concentrates private law, international business, social theory, advanced communication, finance, econometrics and applied research. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

blocks: Both introduce legal systems, fields and the social operation of law; UCR does so comparatively rather than through a Dutch doctrinal sequence.
Both examine rights, justice and legal-philosophical questions; UCR concentrates on human rights and philosophy.
Ethics supports normative reasoning about justice but is not a general jurisprudence course.
Both examine constitutional institutions, public powers and legal limits; UCR compares systems rather than teaching Dutch doctrine.
UCR has no separate advanced Dutch administrative-law course.
Comparative Constitutional Law is already aligned to the common public-law introduction; UCR has no second dedicated constitutional-law course.
Foundations of European Union Law is already aligned to the common EU-law introduction; UCR has no second dedicated EU-law course.
Both introduce private-law rights and obligations; UCR surveys contract, property, family and related relationships rather than a Dutch doctrinal sequence.
Both introduce substantive criminal-law reasoning and criminal justice, including accountability and safeguards.
UCR Principles of Private Law includes property but is already aligned to the obligations component and does not form a second dedicated property course.
UCR has no second advanced Dutch property-law course.
UCR Criminal Law & Criminal Justice is already aligned to the introductory component and does not reproduce a second advanced doctrinal course.
UCR Principles of Private Law is already aligned to the introductory obligations component and does not reproduce an advanced Dutch obligations course.
UCR has no dedicated Dutch civil or administrative procedure course.
Both address legal relationships in economic life, but UCR focuses on transnational business law rather than Dutch labour law.
The comparator requires an independent legal graduation project. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so UCR’s optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.
The comparator reserves 45 EC for non-legal profiling. UCR flexibility is distributed across the entire 180-EC programme, so no fixed scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: Utrecht’s Rechtsgeleerdheid is a professional academic Dutch-law degree with a continuous jurisdiction-specific sequence in private, public, criminal, European and international law, procedure, legal research and a graduation project. UCR offers an interdisciplinary law cluster and related politics, sociology, economics, business, history, philosophy and research courses. It does not reproduce the Dutch doctrinal sequence, dedicated procedural subjects or professional qualification path. These pathways compare related legal and institutional fields; none substitutes for the external law degree.
